newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Chun's death sentence cut to life in jail - state TV.
newsitem.headline: Chun's death sentence cut to life in jail - state TV.

text.p: A South Korean Court on Monday commuted the death sentence on former president Chun Doo Hwan to life imprisonment and cut to 17 years from 22-1/2 years the jail term for his successor Roh Tae-woo, state television reported.
The decisions by a three-judge panel in the South Korean High Court drew protest gasps from spectators gathered in the courtroom for the latest twist in the country's "trial of the century."

Chun was sentenced to death in August for mutiny, treason and bribery over a 1979 coup, a massacre in 1980 in the city of Kwangju that crushed democratic opposition and for amassing a slush fund worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
Roh was convicted on similar charges involving the same incidents.

In judging the appeals by the two men against their guilty verdicts, the judges said Chun's death sentence was commuted because of his contribution to economic development and the peaceful transfer of the presidency to Roh in 1988, the Korea Broadcasting System (KBS) said.
Chun, president from 1980 to 1988, was fined 263 billion won ($311.6 million) and Roh, president from 1988 to 1993, was fined 226 billion won, KBS initially reported.
Both men patted each other encouragingly on the knee in the minutes leading up to the court's decision.
They sat awaiting their fate in light blue prison uniforms and white rubber slippers -- Chun as prisoner 3124 and Roh as prisoner 1042.
With them were 14 ex-generals who served under them and also were found guilty at August's trials.
The court upheld the acquital of one general, Park Joon-byoung, KBS said. Prosecutors had been seeking a jail term.
Of the other 13 one-time commanders, the court reduced 12 of their sentences to between 3-1/2 and eight years from between four and 10 years. One sentence of seven years remained unchanged.
All the defendants can make a final appeals to the Supreme Court. President Kim Young-sam also has the power to grant them a pardon.
Later on Monday the High Court will rule on the appeals against bribery convictions by five businessmen and six former aides and bodyguards. (Conversion: $1 = 844 won)
